check:
import os,subprocess,sys
cfg=os.environ.get('CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR') or ''
if not os.path.isdir(cfg): sys.exit('REFUSED: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR %r is not a directory, so no install can be walked' % cfg)
tool=''
for base,_d,files in os.walk(cfg):
    if 'bm_project.py' in files: tool=os.path.join(base,'bm_project.py'); break
if not tool: sys.exit('REFUSED: no bm_project.py under the installed config, so the intake command a stranger is told to run is not installed at all')
home=os.environ.get('HOME') or ''
work=os.path.join(home,'journey-intake')
os.makedirs(work,exist_ok=True)
subprocess.run(['git','init','-q','.'],cwd=work,capture_output=True,text=True)
with open(os.path.join(work,'mathlib.py'),'w') as fh: fh.write('def add(a, b):\n    return a + b\n')
with open(os.path.join(work,'test_mathlib.py'),'w') as fh: fh.write('import mathlib\n\ndef test_add():\n    assert True\n')
r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-B',tool,'adopt','--ask','make the add function handle two strings','--out',os.path.join(work,'contract.json')],cwd=work,capture_output=True,text=True)
said=(r.stdout+r.stderr).strip().splitlines()
print('the installed %s adopt exited %d: %s' % (os.path.basename(tool),r.returncode,said[-1][:150] if said else '(no output)'))
sys.exit(0 if r.returncode==0 else 1)

J5.title: memory: a stranger's notes land in one folder, and one word removes what Brother wrote

_note: JT0's row set: one row per rubric cell of the 2026-10-18 first hour rubric, walked on a FRESH
INSTALL by scripts/journey/run_journey.py. A row declares the atom ids it answers for and, when a
real measurement exists, the argv that measures it.
A ROW WITH NO CHECK READS NO-DATA, NEVER PASS. Several J1 rows are made true and made measurable
by units that have not landed (DOOR1 for the six verb door, README118 for the claims register,
FRUN1 for the first screen's own paths and names). Pointing those rows at the nearest existing
tool would be worse than leaving them unmeasured: scripts/gen_door_table.py --check is a real flag
and it measures whether the door TABLE is fresh, which is not whether the door shows six verbs.
That substitution is the green-but-hollow class the delivery laws name, so each such row carries
measured_by instead, naming the unit that will bring its measurement with it.
J5's first row CARRIES A REAL MEASUREMENT, and it lives in the row because a row's only
measurement seam is an argv list and JT0.e changes one file. It REFUSES, rather than quietly
unsetting, when any of the three vault variables is inherited: measured 2026-10-25 on this
machine, where the owner's BROTHERMODE_VAULT makes resolve answer PASS on the owner's own vault,
so a row that merely ran resolve would read PASS here and FAIL for a stranger. A refusal exits
non zero, which reads FAIL and never PASS.
J5's second row stays unmeasured ON PURPOSE, and the reason is measured rather than assumed:
forget has no declared root list to check against (docs/DATA.md is absent, and door.py defines
neither forget nor data_roots, 0 occurrences of each on 2026-10-25), and the person-only yes it
will take does not exist yet either. Writing a check now would grade FOOT1H against a root list
this file invented, which is the same hollow class as pointing a row at the nearest real flag.
ATOM IDS COME FROM THE CROSSWALK, NEVER FROM THIS FILE'S IMAGINATION. The per journey sets are
BENCHMARK-CROSSWALK.md's own table (J2: U01, U03, U06, W03, E01, V01, V02, V09; J4: U04, U09, W06,
W12, V05; J5: W09, C03, C04) and each id's meaning is the 77 atom scorecard's own row. Which row
inside a journey carries which of its atoms is an ASSIGNMENT made here and checkable against those
two sources; it is not itself a measurement. J5's ids were wrong when first written (A07 and S04 are
in no register, only in one seat's log) and are corrected here.
J2 CARRIES TWO REAL CHECKS. A.adopt-exits-0 runs the INSTALLED bm_project.py, found BY NAME under
the installed config rather than at a hardcoded cache path, in a throwaway git repository shaped like
the README's toy one. Running the repository's own copy instead would read PASS and hide the shipped
defect: measured 2026-10-25, adopt exits 0 from this tree, where contract_check.py sits beside it,
and that adjacency is exactly what a plugin install does not reproduce.
C.no-pass-for-unrun-check reads the record intake wrote and fails when a commanded check carries a
PASS whose only evidence is a file: range, which is the source of the test rather than a run of it.
The receipt contract's own words are that a check carries the command that ran it and that command's
exit code, so a source range is not one. It REFUSES when the record declares no commanded check at
all, because a repository with no checks must never read as a pass here.

cannot be walked yet. Five of them need a whole run through the door, and the zero model route for
